# DSH Vibeify
**Turn your AI work into a living magazine.**
DSH Vibeify is an open-source, local magazine for DeepSeek Harness. It gives AI work a visual, conte
nt-first home: use DeepSeek, ChatGPT, or both; keep Chat for control; and share only the finished ar
e DeepSeek, ChatGPT, or both; keep Chat for control; and share only the finished article you choose.
Vibeify 0.17.1 improves magazine-card and image recovery while retaining **DeepSeek-led with OpenAI
support**: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 leads through `deepseek-flash`, with GPT-6.1 Sol available for b
ounded tasks through ChatGPT-authenticated Codex. This mode uses Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 and Codex 0.164.
0. See the installation route.

works · Get installation help · Email Vibeify
The real 2:24 demonstration opens Vibe with content, turns a Chat request into a visual card, uses a
n explicit Update, then previews one article privately before optional publication. Watch it on YouT
plicit Update, then previews one article privately before optional publication. Watch it on YouTube.
DSH Vibeify's magazine is **not** a public website. It turns DeepSeek Harness—a local runtime for ag
ents, models, tools, permissions and sessions—into a creator-first streaming experience that *behave
s* like a website. Vibe is the visual, content-first home; Chat remains underneath for detailed requ
ests, progress, approvals, Queue, Steer and technical evidence. An optional, deliberately separate s
hare service can publish one reviewed article at a time without exposing the local magazine or requi
ring the recipient to have DSH, ChatGPT, or DeepSeek.
## The idea: generative AI beyond turn-by-turn chat
Most AI products begin with an empty box. The person writes a prompt, waits for one answer, and repe
ats. DSH Vibeify begins with something useful to explore and turns Chat work from any thread into on
e continuous edition. Returning readers open their saved edition, newest stories first. A configured
editorial direction takes precedence over the local welcome issue. First-time readers without a dir
ection can still explore local orientation pages without a model call; **Update my magazine** or **U
pdate VIBE now** requests a fresh people-centred issue. **Look & feel** controls the magazine palett
e, text size and spacing separately from Chat. For an explicit public-content request, each complete
verified card can arrive while the rest of the answer is still being made; ordinary final answers j
oin after completion. It generates extra magazine material only when the reader asks for an update.
> **The one sentence to remember:** open Chat and say **“Make a Vibe about…”** when you want a delib
erately edited Vibe article or series. That explicit wording tells the active DSH lead to use Vibeif
y's visual, linked, complete-chunk publishing contract. An ordinary Chat answer may still join Vibe
after it finishes, but it is not guaranteed to receive the richer article structure or to stream car
d by card while the turn is running.

The visible surface is website-like, but the machinery underneath is an agent harness:
| Layer | What it does |
| **DSH** | Runs sessions, agents, model routes, tools, permissions and approvals on the user's mach

ine. |
| **Vibeify** | Adds the continuous editorial stream, visual presentation, local content buff

er and safe route between generated work and the stream. |
| **Vibe** | Presents every thread's comp
leted answers—and complete verified cards from an active public-content request—as one newest-first
edition. A hidden local reserve may be prepared while Vibe is in recent use; only Pull to update, Up
date, a closed public-content card, or a completed Chat answer changes the visible magazine. It is n

ot a separate public site. |
[该节后续省略]
## Play inside the article
Ask Chat to **“Make a Vibe with an embedded game, calculator, form or interactive graph.”** Self-con
tained interactive panels appear within the article. Open a panel to use it while reading; the built
-in Mochi Meadow game is visible immediately and starts only when you press its start button.
[该节后续省略]
## Contact
For Vibeify questions, installation help, or responsible reports that should not begin in a public i
ssue, email info@codingforjustice.org.uk. Do not send passwords, API keys, cookies, OAuth tokens, pr
ivate prompts, session exports, or unreviewed logs.
## What you get
- **A continuous, website-like local magazine.** Vibe covers the DSH work surface completely and ope
ns directly into one long, responsive edition. There is no catalogue-to-player-to-result transition.
- **A welcome issue that sells the choice again.** Twenty-one visual, reader-facing panels explain
the benefits and everyday use of Vibe, Chat, deliberate updates, editorial direction, local learning
, imagery, saving, sharing, Queue/Steer, Think/Trajectory, connected apps, DSH, plugins, open source
, provider and capability choices, permissions and safe updates. Each panel offers a concrete prompt
and a direct route into Chat. The issue is rebuilt from the active plugin rather than cached, so an

upgrade cannot reopen with last version's onboarding.
- **A deep, findable local well.** Twenty-fou
r deterministic editorial chunks—text, credited photography and AI-assisted graphics—are available s
ynchronously on a cold visit. Every tile receives one of twelve bundled visuals with varied crop and
treatment, later images decode lazily, and up to 160 completed magazine items persist for 30 days.
**Find Vibes** searches their titles and article text locally; 96 places inside the same total are p

rotected for completed Chat-made Vibes so editorial refills cannot crowd all of them out.
- **Instan
t, bounded updates.** Pull down from the top of Vibe—including a two-finger pull on a Mac trackpad—o
r choose **Update**. Ready pages are released from the hidden reserve synchronously; a local visual
short ensures an immediate response even when the reserve is empty. If fewer than four ready pages e
xist, one bounded foreground batch fills the gap and streams complete pages independently. **Stop up

date** cancels only that dedicated foreground turn, and a 20-minute ceiling stops a stuck update.
